name: Software Supply-Chain Security
description: Security of dependencies, package registries, build systems, CI/CD, and code provenance.
narrative:
The earliest USENIX Security work in this list approached supply-chain concerns mostly from the trust and provenance angles rather than from package ecosystems directly. "The Broken Shield: Measuring Revocation Effectiveness in the Windows Code-Signing PKI" (2018) probed whether the code-signing trust infrastructure that vouches for distributed binaries actually worked, while "in-toto: Providing farm-to-table guarantees for bits and bytes" (2019) offered a foundational framework for cryptographically verifying that every step of the build pipeline was performed by the right actor in the right order. In the same window, "Small World with High Risks: A Study of Security Threats in the npm Ecosystem" (2019) reframed the problem at scale, showing how deep transitive dependency trees in npm let a handful of maintainers or compromised packages put enormous swaths of the software world at risk.

The early 2020s brought a shift from measuring trust toward attacking and defending the artifacts and registries themselves. Researchers began dissecting how malicious packages reach developers: "Exploring the Unchartered Space of Container Registry Typosquatting" (2022) and later "Beyond Typosquatting: An In-depth Look at Package Confusion" (2023) systematized the naming-based tricks attackers use to get the wrong dependency installed. In parallel, "Mining Node.js Vulnerabilities via Object Dependence Graph and Query" (2022) pushed program-analysis techniques into the ecosystem to surface vulnerable packages automatically.

A second major thread that matured in this period was the build and CI/CD layer, increasingly recognized as a high-value target. "Characterizing the Security of Github CI Workflows" (2022) and "ARGUS: A Framework for Staged Static Taint Analysis of GitHub Workflows and Actions" (2023) moved the community from anecdote to systematic, analysis-driven understanding of how automated pipelines leak secrets and execute untrusted code.

Most recently the field has leaned heavily on machine learning and behavioral analysis to detect malicious packages in real time across the dominant ecosystems. "DONAPI: Malicious NPM Packages Detector using Behavior Sequence Knowledge Mapping" (2024) and "MalGuard: Towards Real-Time, Accurate, and Actionable Detection of Malicious Packages in PyPI Ecosystem" (2025) mark where the area stands now: scalable, actionable detectors aimed squarely at npm and PyPI, complementing the earlier provenance- and registry-trust foundations rather than replacing them.

milestones.title: The Broken Shield: Measuring Revocation Effectiveness in the Windows Code-Signing PKI
milestones.note: exposed weaknesses in the code-signing trust infrastructure that underpins distributed software provenance

milestones.title: in-toto: Providing farm-to-table guarantees for bits and bytes
milestones.note: introduced a foundational framework for cryptographically verifying integrity across every step of the software build pipeline

milestones.title: Small World with High Risks: A Study of Security Threats in the npm Ecosystem
milestones.note: quantified how deep transitive dependencies make package ecosystems systemically fragile, defining the npm threat model

milestones.title: Characterizing the Security of Github CI Workflows
milestones.note: first systematic security characterization of CI/CD pipelines as a distinct supply-chain attack surface

milestones.title: Beyond Typosquatting: An In-depth Look at Package Confusion
milestones.note: broadened understanding of name-based dependency-confusion attacks beyond simple typosquatting

milestones.title: ARGUS: A Framework for Staged Static Taint Analysis of GitHub Workflows and Actions
milestones.note: brought scalable static taint analysis to GitHub Actions, operationalizing CI/CD vulnerability discovery

milestones.title: DONAPI: Malicious NPM Packages Detector using Behavior Sequence Knowledge Mapping
milestones.note: advanced behavior-based detection of malicious npm packages using knowledge-mapped behavior sequences

milestones.title: MalGuard: Towards Real-Time, Accurate, and Actionable Detection of Malicious Packages in PyPI Ecosystem
milestones.note: marks the current real-time, actionable detection frontier for malicious packages in PyPI
